name: Standing Deep Breathing (Pranayama)
setup: Stand tall with feet together, interlace your fingers and tuck your knuckles under your chin.
instructions: Inhale slowly through your nose for six counts, raising your elbows up beside your ears like wings while your knuckles stay under your chin.
Exhale through your mouth for six counts, dropping your head back and bringing your elbows and forearms together in front of your face.
Keep your knees relaxed and your spine long throughout.
Repeat for the prescribed number of slow breath cycles.

name: Half Moon Pose with Hands to Feet (Ardha Chandrasana with Pada Hastasana)
setup: Stand with feet together, raise your arms overhead and interlace your fingers in a steeple grip with index fingers extended.
instructions: Press your hips to the left and bend your whole torso to the right in one unbroken line, arms glued to your ears. Hold and breathe.
Return to centre and repeat the side bend to the left.
Return to centre, then hinge back from the hips into a gentle standing backbend, pushing your hips forward.
Come up, fold forward and take hold of your heels from behind, drawing your chest to your thighs with elbows behind your calves.

name: Awkward Pose (Utkatasana)
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart and parallel, arms extended forward at shoulder height, palms down.
instructions: Part one: sit down as if into an invisible chair until your thighs are parallel to the floor, spine upright. Hold.
Part two: rise onto the balls of your feet, then sit again with hips hovering at knee height, balancing on your toes. Hold.
Part three: with knees together on tiptoes, lower your hips all the way to your heels and hold, spine tall.
Keep your arms reaching forward and breathe steadily through every stage.

name: Eagle Pose (Garudasana)
setup: Stand tall and sweep your right arm under your left, wrapping the forearms so your palms meet.
instructions: Sit your hips down and back, then lift your right leg over your left thigh, hooking the foot behind the left calf if possible.
Pull your wrapped elbows down and away from your face while sinking lower into the standing leg.
Square your hips and shoulders forward, fix your gaze on one point and hold, breathing evenly.
Unwind slowly and repeat on the other side.

name: Standing Head to Knee (Dandayamana Janushirasana)
setup: Stand on your left leg, lock the knee, and interlace all ten fingers around the sole of your right foot, lifting the knee toward your chest.
instructions: Keeping the standing knee locked, slowly kick your right leg forward until it is parallel to the floor.
Tuck your elbows down beside your calf and round forward, bringing your forehead toward your knee.
Hold with steady breath, standing leg solid as a lamp post.
Reverse out with the same control and repeat on the other side. Only progress to each stage when the previous one is stable.

name: Standing Bow Pose (Dandayamana Dhanurasana)
setup: Stand on your left leg. Reach your right hand back and grip the inside of your right foot; extend your left arm straight up beside your ear.
instructions: Kick your right foot up and back into your hand while your torso and left arm tilt forward as a counterbalance.
Keep kicking until your body forms a standing bow, chest level with the floor and back leg rising high behind you.
Keep both shoulders rotating square to the front and your gaze fixed ahead.
Release with control and repeat on the other side.

name: Balancing Stick Pose (Tuladandasana)
setup: Stand tall, arms overhead with palms together and index fingers steepled, and step your right foot one stride forward.
instructions: Hinge forward from the hips in one piece, lifting your left leg behind you until body and leg form a straight horizontal line.
Stretch forward through your fingertips and back through your pointed toes — one unbroken line like a capital T.
Keep your hips level and both knees locked; breathe steadily for the hold.
Return upright with control and repeat on the other leg.

name: Standing Separate Leg Stretching Pose (Dandayamana Bibhaktapada Paschimotthanasana)
setup: Step your feet wide apart, about one leg-length, toes turned slightly in.
instructions: Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back and take hold of the outside edges of your feet.
Pull gently with your arms, drawing the crown of your head toward the floor between your feet.
Keep your weight in the balls of your feet and your legs straight.
Hold and breathe, letting the hamstrings and inner thighs release.

name: Triangle Pose (Trikanasana)
setup: Step your feet wide apart, turn your right foot out 90 degrees, and extend both arms to shoulder height.
instructions: Bend your right knee to a right angle so the thigh is parallel to the floor.
Tilt your torso sideways, placing your right fingertips lightly at your right big toe while your left arm reaches straight up.
Turn your head to gaze at the raised hand, chest and hips staying open to the side.
Press both feet firmly into the floor, hold and breathe, then repeat on the other side.

name: Standing Separate Leg Head to Knee Pose (Dandayamana Bibhaktapada Janushirasana)
setup: From a wide stance, turn your whole body to face your right foot, hips square, arms overhead with palms together.
instructions: Tuck your chin to your chest and round down, bringing your forehead toward your right knee.
Bend the front knee as much as needed so forehead and knee stay in contact.
Keep your arms framing your head and your back foot grounded.
Compress, breathe, come up with a flat strong body, and repeat on the other side.

name: Tree Pose (Tadasana Vrksasana)
setup: Stand tall on your left leg and draw your right foot up, placing the sole high against your inner left thigh.
instructions: Press the foot and thigh gently into each other and let your right knee open to the side.
Bring your palms together in front of your chest, or reach them overhead.
Lengthen through the crown of your head, fix your gaze on a still point, and breathe.
Hold steadily, then change legs.

name: Toe Stand Pose (Padangustasana)
setup: From Tree Pose with your right foot on your left thigh, fix your gaze on a point on the floor about a metre ahead.
instructions: Hinge forward and bend the standing leg, lowering your hips with control until you balance on the ball of your left foot.
Sit your hips down onto your raised left heel, spine tall, then bring your palms together at your chest.
Balance with steady breath, knees in one line.
Press back up through the standing leg and repeat on the other side.

name: Dead Body Pose (Savasana)
setup: Lie flat on your back with heels together, feet relaxed open, arms by your sides with palms facing up.
instructions: Close your eyes and let your whole body become completely heavy and still.
Breathe naturally through your nose, releasing tension from your face, shoulders and hands.
Stay perfectly still and present for the prescribed time.

name: Wind Removing Pose (Pavanamuktasana)
setup: Lie flat on your back with legs extended.
instructions: Draw your right knee toward your right shoulder and interlace your fingers below the knee, pulling it gently down. Hold and breathe.
Switch and hug the left knee toward the left shoulder. Hold.
Finally draw both knees to your chest, wrapping your arms around your shins, and let your lower back release into the floor.
Keep your shoulders and head relaxed on the ground throughout.

name: Bikram Sit-Up
setup: Lie on your back with legs extended, feet flexed, arms stretched overhead with biceps by your ears.
instructions: Inhale, then sit up in one motion with arms staying beside your ears.
Exhale sharply in two bursts as you fold forward and reach for your flexed toes.
Keep your legs locked and lengthen your spine over your legs.
Roll back down with control to begin the next rep.

name: Cobra Pose (Bhujangasana)
setup: Lie on your stomach with legs together, palms flat under your shoulders, elbows hugged into your ribs.
instructions: Using your back muscles more than your arms, peel your chest off the floor to navel height.
Roll your shoulders down and back, elbows staying bent and close to your body.
Press the tops of your feet and hips into the floor; gaze gently upward.
Hold with steady breath, then lower slowly.

name: Locust Pose (Salabhasana)
setup: Lie on your stomach with your chin on the floor and arms straight beneath your body, palms down under your hips.
instructions: Keeping both hips on your hands, lift your right leg straight up as high as possible. Hold, then lower and lift the left leg.
For the final stage, press into your arms and lift both legs together off the floor, knees locked.
Keep your chin on the floor and shoulders touching the ground.
Lower slowly and rest a breath between stages.

name: Full Locust Pose (Poorna Salabhasana)
setup: Lie on your stomach with arms out to the sides at shoulder height like aeroplane wings, palms down, legs together.
instructions: In one motion lift your chest, arms and legs off the floor, flying upward from the waist.
Reach your fingertips back like wingtips and keep your legs together and locked.
Lift your chin and gaze forward; only your hips and lower belly stay on the floor.
Hold with strong steady breath, then release down slowly.

name: Bow Pose (Dhanurasana)
setup: Lie on your stomach, bend both knees and reach back to grip the outside of each foot near the toes.
instructions: Kick your feet up and back into your hands, letting the kick lift your chest and thighs off the floor.
Balance on your abdomen, body curved like an archer's bow, arms straight like the bowstring.
Lift your chin and roll your weight gently with the breath.
Release with control, lowering chest and knees together.

name: Fixed Firm Pose (Supta Vajrasana)
setup: Kneel with your knees together and sit your hips on the floor between your heels, feet hugging your hips.
instructions: Walk your hands back behind you and lower onto your elbows, keeping both knees on the floor.
If comfortable, lower your back and shoulders all the way to the floor and reach your arms overhead, holding opposite elbows.
Let the front of your thighs lengthen; breathe slowly into your belly.
Come up the same way you went down — onto elbows first, never twisting.

name: Half Tortoise Pose (Ardha Kurmasana)
setup: Kneel and sit back on your heels, then raise your arms overhead with palms together and thumbs crossed.
instructions: Keeping hips on your heels, hinge forward from the hips in one straight line until your little fingers and forehead touch the floor.
Stretch your arms as far forward as possible, lengthening through the sides of your body.
Relax your neck and breathe deeply into your back.
Come up in one piece with arms still beside your ears.

name: Camel Pose (Ustrasana)
setup: Kneel upright with knees and feet hip-width apart, hands supporting your lower back, fingers pointing down.
instructions: Lift your chest and arch back slowly, pushing your hips forward over your knees.
When ready, reach back and place your palms on your heels, letting your head drop gently back.
Keep pressing the hips forward so the bend spreads along your whole spine.
Hold with open breath, then bring your hands back to your hips and rise with care.

name: Rabbit Pose (Sasangasana)
setup: Kneel sitting on your heels and grip your heels firmly with your hands, thumbs outside.
instructions: Tuck your chin and curl forward, placing the top of your head on the floor against your knees.
Lift your hips toward the ceiling, rolling forward like a wheel until your arms are straight.
Keep a firm grip on your heels and your forehead touching your knees, spine rounding into a full stretch.
Breathe into your upper back, then unroll slowly, head coming up last.

name: Head to Knee Pose with Stretching Pose (Janushirasana with Paschimotthanasana)
setup: Sit with your right leg extended and your left foot tucked against your right inner thigh.
instructions: Turn your torso over the straight leg, grip your flexed right foot with both hands and bring your forehead toward your knee, bending the knee if needed.
Hold, breathe, then repeat on the other side.
For the stretching stage, extend both legs together, grip your feet and fold your whole torso forward over your legs.
Pull gently with the arms while keeping the spine long; let the head release last.

name: Spine Twisting Pose (Ardha Matsyendrasana)
setup: Sit with your left knee bent on the floor and step your right foot over the left thigh, planting it flat.
instructions: Place your right hand on the floor behind you and hook your left elbow outside your right knee.
Inhale to lengthen your spine tall, then exhale and twist your torso to the right, looking over your right shoulder.
Deepen the twist gently with each exhale, hips staying grounded.
Unwind slowly and repeat on the other side.

name: Blowing in Firm Pose (Kapalbhati in Vajrasana)
setup: Kneel sitting on your heels with your spine tall and palms resting on your knees.
instructions: Exhale forcefully through your mouth with a sharp snap of the belly button toward the spine.
Let the inhale happen passively between blows — only the exhale is active.
Keep your shoulders, face and arms relaxed; only the abdomen moves.
Continue at a steady rhythm for the prescribed number of breaths.

name: Downward Facing Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana)
setup: Start on all fours with hands shoulder-width apart, fingers spread, toes tucked.
instructions: Lift your hips up and back until your body forms an inverted V.
Press the floor away through your whole hands, letting your head hang relaxed between your arms.
Reach your heels toward the floor with a soft bend in the knees if needed, spine staying long.
Hold and breathe deeply, pedalling the feet gently if it helps the legs release.

name: Upward Facing Dog (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana)
setup: Lie face down with palms beside your lower ribs and the tops of your feet on the floor.
instructions: Press into your hands and straighten your arms, lifting your chest and your thighs off the floor.
Only your palms and the tops of your feet touch the ground; shoulders roll down away from your ears.
Open your chest forward and upward, gaze slightly lifted.
Hold with steady breath, then lower or push back into Downward Dog.

name: Wheel Pose (Urdhva Dhanurasana)
setup: Lie on your back, bend your knees with feet flat near your hips, and place your palms on the floor beside your ears, fingers pointing toward your shoulders.
instructions: Press into hands and feet and lift your hips, pausing briefly with the crown of your head lightly on the floor.
Straighten your arms and legs together, arching your whole body into a high backbend.
Push the floor away, letting your chest move toward the wall behind you and your head hang free.
Hold with strong breath, then tuck your chin and lower down slowly with control.

name: Dancer's Pose (Natarajasana)
setup: Stand tall on your left leg, bend your right knee and grip the inside of your right ankle behind you.
instructions: Reach your left arm forward and up as you press your right foot back and up into your hand.
Let your chest tilt slightly forward as the back leg rises, body opening into a graceful standing backbend.
Square your hips toward the front and fix your gaze past your reaching fingertips.
Hold with poise and steady breath, then lower slowly and repeat on the other side.

name: Warrior I (Virabhadrasana I)
setup: From standing, step your left foot back about a leg-length, back foot angled out 45 degrees, hips squared to the front.
instructions: Bend your right knee until it stacks over the ankle, thigh moving toward parallel.
Sweep both arms overhead, palms facing each other, shoulders relaxed away from the ears.
Press the outer edge of the back foot down and lift through the chest.
Hold and breathe, then switch sides.

name: Warrior II (Virabhadrasana II)
setup: Step your feet wide apart, turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left toes slightly in, hips opening to the side.
instructions: Bend your right knee over the ankle while the back leg stays straight and strong.
Extend your arms parallel to the floor, reaching actively front and back.
Keep your torso vertical and centred between your legs; gaze over the front fingertips.
Sink and hold with steady breath, then repeat on the other side.

name: Warrior III (Virabhadrasana III)
setup: Stand on your right leg with your arms extended overhead, palms facing each other.
instructions: Hinge forward from the hips, lifting your left leg straight behind you until torso, arms and leg form one horizontal line.
Keep your hips level — the lifted leg's toes point straight down.
Reach long through fingertips and heel in opposite directions, gaze at the floor just ahead.
Hold with steady balance, then rise and change sides.

name: Reverse Warrior (Viparita Virabhadrasana)
setup: Begin in Warrior II with your right knee bent and arms extended.
instructions: Flip your right palm up and reach the arm overhead as your torso leans back into a gentle side bend.
Let your left hand rest lightly on your back leg without putting weight into it.
Keep the front knee bent and sinking — the legs do not move as the torso arcs.
Breathe into the long right side of your body, then repeat on the other side.

name: Extended Side Angle Pose (Utthita Parsvakonasana)
setup: From Warrior II with your right knee bent, prepare to tilt your torso toward the front leg.
instructions: Lower your right forearm onto your right thigh, or your fingertips to the floor outside the front foot.
Sweep your left arm over your ear, creating one long line from back heel to fingertips.
Spiral your chest open toward the ceiling, gazing up under the raised arm.
Press through the outer edge of the back foot, hold, then switch sides.

name: Half Moon Balance (Ardha Chandrasana)
setup: From a forward fold over your right leg, place your right fingertips on the floor (or a block) about 30 cm ahead of your toes.
instructions: Shift your weight into the right leg and float your left leg up behind you to hip height.
Stack your hips and shoulders sideways, opening your whole body to the left.
Extend your left arm straight up and, if balanced, turn your gaze toward it.
Hold with steady breath, lower with control, and repeat on the other side.

name: Pigeon Pose (Eka Pada Rajakapotasana)
setup: From all fours, slide your right knee forward behind your right wrist, shin angled across the mat, and extend your left leg straight back.
instructions: Square your hips toward the floor, letting them sink evenly — pad the right hip if it lifts.
Stay upright on your fingertips for a deeper hip opening, or fold your torso forward over the front shin.
Relax your shoulders and breathe slowly into the stretch in your outer hip and glute.
Walk your hands back, step out, and repeat on the other side.

name: Bridge Pose (Setu Bandha Sarvangasana)
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart close to your hips, arms alongside your body.
instructions: Press into your feet and lift your hips toward the ceiling, rolling up through the spine.
Interlace your fingers under your back and walk your shoulders together beneath you.
Keep your knees tracking straight ahead and your chest lifting toward your chin.
Hold with smooth breath, then release the hands and roll down one vertebra at a time.

name: Boat Pose (Navasana)
setup: Sit with knees bent, feet flat, hands lightly behind your knees, spine long.
instructions: Lean back slightly and float your feet off the floor, shins parallel to the ground.
Extend your arms forward at shoulder height, palms facing in.
For the full pose, straighten your legs so your body forms a V; keep your chest lifted, never rounding.
Hold with steady breath, lower with control.

name: Crow Pose (Bakasana)
setup: Squat down and plant your palms shoulder-width apart on the floor, fingers spread wide.
instructions: Bend your elbows slightly and snug your knees high onto the backs of your upper arms.
Shift your weight forward onto your hands, gazing at a point ahead of your fingertips — never straight down.
Lift one foot, then the other, balancing with your heels drawing toward your hips.
Hold with the core gripping strongly, then lower your feet softly back to the floor.

name: Four-Limbed Staff Pose (Chaturanga Dandasana)
setup: Begin in a strong high plank with shoulders stacked over wrists and body in one line.
instructions: Shift slightly forward onto your toes, then bend your elbows straight back, hugging them against your ribs.
Lower in one piece until your upper arms are parallel to the floor — no lower.
Keep your shoulders level with your elbows and your body rigid from head to heels.
Hold the hover with steady breath, then push back up or move into Upward Dog.

name: Happy Baby Pose (Ananda Balasana)
setup: Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your armpits, shins vertical.
instructions: Grip the outside edges of your feet with your hands, knees staying wide of your torso.
Gently pull your feet down so your knees draw toward the floor beside your ribs.
Keep your tailbone and shoulders melting into the floor.
Rock softly side to side if it feels good, breathing slowly throughout.

name: Low Lunge (Anjaneyasana)
setup: From a lunge with your right foot forward, lower your left knee to the floor and untuck the toes.
instructions: Let your hips sink forward and down until you feel a deep stretch along the front of the left hip and thigh.
Sweep both arms overhead, lifting through the chest.
Keep the front knee over the ankle and the tailbone gently tucked.
Hold and breathe, then switch sides.

name: Legs-Up-the-Wall Pose (Viparita Karani)
setup: Sit sideways against a wall, then swing your legs up the wall as you lie back, hips close to or touching the base.
instructions: Rest your legs vertically against the wall, arms relaxed by your sides, palms up.
Let your whole back release into the floor and your breath slow.
Stay for the prescribed time, letting the legs drain and the nervous system settle.
Bend your knees and roll to one side to come out.

name: Puppy Pose (Uttana Shishosana)
setup: Start on all fours with hips stacked over knees.
instructions: Keeping your hips high over your knees, walk your hands far forward and melt your chest toward the floor.
Rest your forehead (or chin) on the mat, arms active and reaching.
Let your heart sink and your upper back open with each exhale.
Walk the hands back under your shoulders to come out.

name: Thread the Needle Stretch
setup: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
instructions: Slide your right arm palm-up underneath your left arm, lowering your right shoulder and ear to the floor.
Let your upper back rotate while your hips stay high and square.
Press lightly through the left hand to deepen the twist between your shoulder blades.
Breathe into the stretch, unwind, and repeat on the other side.

name: Butterfly Stretch
setup: Sit tall and bring the soles of your feet together, letting your knees fall open.
instructions: Hold your feet or ankles and draw your heels comfortably toward your hips.
Sit tall through the spine, then hinge gently forward from the hips for a deeper stretch.
Let gravity ease the knees toward the floor — never bounce or press them down.
Hold and breathe slowly into the inner thighs.

name: Frog Stretch
setup: On a padded surface, come to all fours and slide your knees wide apart, ankles in line with the knees, feet flexed and turned out.
instructions: Lower onto your forearms and slowly rock your hips back toward your heels.
Stop where the inner-thigh stretch is strong but breathable, keeping the spine neutral.
Rock gently forward and back, or simply hold at your edge.
Walk your knees together carefully to come out.

name: Scorpion Stretch
setup: Lie face down with arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms down.
instructions: Bend your right knee and sweep your right foot up and across your body toward your left hand.
Let your right hip lift and rotate while your chest and arms stay anchored to the floor.
Pause at the end range, feeling the stretch through your hip flexor, trunk and chest.
Return slowly and alternate sides at a controlled pace.

name: Sleeper Stretch
setup: Lie on your right side with your right arm straight out from the shoulder and the elbow bent to 90 degrees, fingers pointing up.
instructions: With your left hand, gently press your right forearm down toward the floor, rotating the shoulder internally.
Keep your shoulder blade pinned beneath you and your torso from rolling backward.
Press only to a gentle stretch at the back of the shoulder — never into pain.
Hold, release slowly, and repeat on the other side.

name: Band Shoulder Dislocates
setup: Hold a light resistance band in front of your thighs with a grip wide enough that there is gentle tension.
instructions: With straight arms, raise the band up and over your head in a wide arc until it touches behind your hips.
Reverse the arc back over your head to the front.
Keep both arms straight and the movement slow — widen your grip if it pinches.
Gradually narrow the grip over weeks as your shoulders open up.

name: Cossack Squat
setup: Stand with your feet in a very wide stance, toes pointing slightly out, arms reaching forward for balance.
instructions: Shift your weight onto your right leg and sit down into a deep squat over that side, left leg staying straight with toes pulling up toward the ceiling.
Keep the right heel planted and your chest as upright as possible.
Push back up through the right leg to the wide stance.
Flow smoothly across to the other side and alternate with control.

name: Jefferson Curl
setup: Stand tall on a low box or step holding a light dumbbell in both hands in front of your thighs.
instructions: Tuck your chin and roll down one vertebra at a time, letting the weight hang and pull you gently toward your toes.
Keep your legs straight and your hips stacked over your heels as your spine curls into a full stretch.
Pause briefly at your end range without forcing depth.
Re-stack the spine slowly from the tailbone up, head arriving last. Keep the load light — this is a mobility drill, not a lift.

name: Wall Angels
setup: Stand with your back, head and hips against a wall, feet a short step away, and press your lower back gently toward the wall.
instructions: Place your arms against the wall in a goalpost position: elbows bent 90 degrees at shoulder height, backs of hands touching the wall.
Slowly slide your arms up the wall as far as you can without anything peeling away.
Slide them back down, drawing the elbows toward your ribs.
Move slowly and keep ribs down and contact constant throughout.
